full_judgment: 35. The earliest and one of the most leading cases in the subject under reference in this Sub- Continent, is the Charanjit Lars case reported in AIR 1951 (SC) 41. Relevant facts are-A share-holder questioned constitutionality of Sholapur Spinning and Weaving Company (Emergency Provision) Act, 1950, which was made for taking over its management on the grounds of mismanagement in the light of Article 14 of the Constitution of India, stating that it is a piece of discriminatory legislation, creates inequality before the law and violates the principle of equal protection of the laws. Among 5 of their Lordships namely, Kania, C.J., Fazlu Ali, Patanjali Sastri, B.K. Mukherjee and S.R. Das, JJ. 4 of their Lordships expressed their respective mind, writing out separate judgments, however, concerning the view taken in the main judgment of Fazl Ali J, that the impugned Act did not infringe the fundamental right provided under Article 14 of the Constitution of India.
